note: Real piers/terminals with verified traffic missing from canonical Korea corridor set. approx_latlon requires verification before geometry binding — nobody invents a pier.

gaps.name: Busan Port International Passenger Terminal (부산항국제여객터미널, North Port)
gaps.why: THE demand anchor of the Busan water market and absent from the corridor list: 938,781 int'l ferry pax in 2025 (T1), 1.4M+ in 2018. All Japan routes sail from here, not the (dormant) coastal terminal. Any Busan network should bind to this terminal.

gaps.name: Busan -> Tsushima (Hitakatsu / Izuhara, Japan) corridor
gaps.why: Largest single cross-border flow out of Busan — 540,185 pax in 2025, 388,229 in 2024, 830,237 in 2018 (T1) — bigger than Busan-Fukuoka, yet missing from the corridor list. Short (~26-49 nm) high-speed craft route, well matched to fast electric vessels.

gaps.name: Busan -> Shimonoseki (Bukwan Ferry / 부관훼리) corridor
gaps.why: 164,137 pax in 2025 (T1), stable historic overnight ferry since 1970; missing from corridor list.

gaps.name: Mipo Wharf, Haeundae (미포선착장) — Haeundae cruise
gaps.why: Busan's main operating harbor-tour pier (Oryukdo daytime tour + Gwangan Bridge night tour, ~50-80 min, adult 25,000-28,000 KRW). The named anchor Tiffany21 ceased operating (~2020-21, pier derelict per fnnews), so Mipo is the live urban-cruise demand point. Annual pax not published.

sources.note: Tiffany21 no longer operates; pier abandoned (Dec 2021)

gaps.name: Gaochi Ferry Terminal, Tongyeong (가오치항 여객선터미널, Dosan-myeon)
gaps.why: The actual mainland gateway to Saryangdo (car ferries every ~1h, 40 min crossing, 7,800-8,500 KRW). The payload routes Saryangdo from Busan, but real traffic flows via Gaochi; needed for corridor realism and transfer geometry.

gaps.name: Samdeok Port, Tongyeong (삼덕항, Sanyang-eup)
gaps.why: Busiest Yokjido gateway — 7 car-ferry round trips/day (Yeongdong Haeun, 55 min, 8,600 KRW), more sailings than Tongyeong Ferry Terminal itself. Missing from corridor list.

gaps.name: Jangseungpo Terminal / Oedo-Haegeumgang cruise piers, Geoje (장승포, 와현, 구조라, 도장포)
gaps.why: Geoje's real water-pax demand: cruise boats to Oedo Botania island garden + Haegeumgang. Oedo drew ~1M visitors/yr pre-COVID, ~500k/yr after (all arrive by boat, round-trip cruise 15,000-27,000 KRW + 11,000 entry). Jangseungpo was also the historical Busan-Geoje ferry endpoint. None of this is in the corridor list.

gaps.name: Busan -> Osaka (Panstar Cruise) corridor
gaps.why: 52,448 pax in 2025 (T1) cruise-ferry route from Busan International Terminal; smaller but persistent flow missing from list.

gaps.name: Unjin Port (Moseulpo South Port), Daejeong-eup
gaps.why: THE biggest miss in the payload: gateway for BOTH Marado and Gapado regular ferries — ~535k island visitors in 2024 (~1.07M one-way boardings), daily peaks of 2,800 pax; purpose-built passenger terminal expanded 2018.

gaps.name: Sanisu-dong Port (Songaksan), Daejeong-eup
gaps.why: Second Marado gateway: Songak Ferry runs ~7 round trips/day to Marado (adult RT 21,000 KRW incl. park fee); splits the ~243k/yr Marado demand with Unjin.

gaps.name: Seogwipo Port (pleasure-boat quay & ex-submarine dock)
gaps.why: Main south-coast marine tourism hub: Seogwipo sightseeing cruise, and Asia's first tourist submarine (Daekuk Haejeo, operating to Munseom since 1988; halted Dec 2023 on heritage grounds, re-permitted conditionally 2025). Meaningful, monetizable waterfront traffic missing from list.

gaps.name: Jagunae-pogu / Yongsu-pogu (Gosan, Hangyeong-myeon) — Chagwido cruise
gaps.why: West-coast gap: Chagwido sightseeing cruise (online booking, daily sailings) plus Chagwido yacht/sunset tours with high dolphin-sighting rates; no payload corridor touches the far west coast.

gaps.name: Gimnyeong Port (yacht tour base)
gaps.why: Payload flags Gimnyeong but has no corridor: Gimnyeong Yacht Tour operates daily sailing/dolphin-watching charters on the northeast coast between Jeju City and Jongdal/Seongsan.

gaps.name: Daepo Port / Jungmun (Grand Bleu yacht tour)
gaps.why: Jungmun corridor (rn-ed5d6c0609fe) has no anchor pier in the payload; commercial yacht tours (Grand Bleu) operate from the Jungmun resort coast — the only existing paid marine service on that OD.

sources.publisher: Operator social listing (Grand Bleu, Jungmun tourist complex)

gaps.name: Jeju Ferry Passenger Terminal — Chuja/mainland berths (Pier 2/7)
gaps.why: Terminal is in the payload but its real demand (677k Mokpo + 633k Wando one-way pax 2025, plus Chuja/Jindo/Nokdong services) is not bound to any corridor except the suspended Busan route.

gaps.name: Sammok Wharf (Yeongjongdo) <-> Sindo <-> Jangbongdo ferry
gaps.why: BIGGEST missing corridor in this market: 817,730 ticketed passengers in 2025 (13 sailings/day, car+pax ferries by Sejong Haeun + Hanlim Haeun). Departs Yeongjongdo — directly adjacent to the payload's Yeongjong Island Marina node. CAUTION: Sindo Peace Bridge (Yeongjong-Sindo) opening is expected to cut the Sindo share (~60% of pax); Jangbongdo (~40%, ~327k) remains water-only.

sources.note: 817,730 pax in 2025; 40% visited Jangbongdo; bridge-opening risk detailed

gaps.name: Wolmido Pier + Yeongjong Gueup Baetteo (car/passenger ferry pair)
gaps.why: Active short crossing (15-20 min, adult 3,500 KRW one-way, cars 7,500 KRW) between Incheon's Wolmido waterfront and Yeongjongdo — the real-world analog for the payload's Incheon<->Yeongjong corridor. Ridership declining since Cheongna Sky Bridge opened; local push to convert to tourist loop cruises under Incheon Bridge / Cheongna Sky Bridge.

sources.note: Post-bridge decline + cruise-conversion proposal (no pax figures)

gaps.name: Yeonan Pier cruise wharf + Palmido island (lighthouse tour)
gaps.why: Incheon's tourist cruise base next to the Coastal Passenger Terminal: Palmido landing tour (adult 27,000-35,000 KRW), harbor cruises (adult 24,000 KRW), Wolmido sunset/fireworks cruises. Palmido itself (Korea's first lighthouse) is a proven excursion node not in the corridor list.

sources.note: Official booking site; sunset tour 18,000-25,000 KRW products

gaps.name: Ara Gimpo Passenger Terminal + Sicheon-naru (Ara Waterway cruise stops)
gaps.why: The actual cruise infrastructure on the Ara Waterway: payload uses 'Gimpo Ara Marina' but the passenger base is Ara Gimpo Terminal (1,358t / 1,000-pax Hyundai Cruise vessel), turning at Sicheon-naru. Also runs the only lock-transit cruise into the Han River (to Yeouido) — proof the Gimpo<->Seoul water link is navigable and licensed.

sources.note: Gimpo T-Sicheon-naru 30,000 KRW RT; Gimpo T->Yeouido lock cruise 25,000 KRW one-way
Cruise segment ~13 km of the 18 km waterway

gaps.name: Seoul Forest temporary wharf (Hangang Bus)
gaps.why: New Hangang Bus stop opened 2026-06-08 for the Seoul Intl Garden Expo: 9,247 riders in first 16 days. Matches the payload's 'Seoul Forest Wharf' — evidence it is now live (temporary status; permanence TBD).

gaps.name: Gaochi Passenger Ferry Terminal (가오치항) <-> Saryangdo Geumpyeong (금평항)
gaps.why: The actual Saryangdo corridor — payload pairs Gaochi with Yeosu (no such service). Two car ferries (420/520 pax), hourly-ish service, T1 tariff available; Saryangdo draws 100k-330k visitors/yr.

sources.note: Terminal at Tongyeong Dosan-myeon, Dosaniju-ro 542-55; lat/lon approximate (±1km)

gaps.name: Junghwa Port (중화항, Sanyang-eup) <-> Yokjido
gaps.why: Cheapest/shortest Yokjido access (adult ~7,600 KRW one-way, Daeil Haeun); carries a large share of Yokji car+pax traffic but absent from payload.

gaps.name: Dolsan Singi Port / Geumodo-Birenggil Ferry Terminal (신기항) <-> Geumodo Yeocheon
gaps.why: Busiest single route in the Yeosu system (24.7% of all Yeosu-area coastal ferry pax in 2016; 243k pax in 2011, growing). Payload routes Geumodo only to Yeosu terminal/Tongyeong.

sources.note: Address: Yeosu Dolsan-eup Singi-gil 90; lat/lon approximate (±1.5km)

gaps.name: Geoje Oedo/Haegeumgang cruise piers: Jangseungpo (장승포), Gujora (구조라), Dojangpo (도장포/바람의언덕)
gaps.why: ~1M cruise customers/yr (≈2M one-way boardings) to Oedo Botania + Haegeumgang — the largest verified water-transit demand pool on the south coast, entirely missing from payload. Jangseungpo alone runs 7-10 vessels.

sources.note: Jangseungpo coords given; Gujora ≈ [34.827, 128.690], Dojangpo ≈ [34.762, 128.679]; all approximate (±1km)

gaps.name: Tongyeong Donam cruise terminal (통영유람선터미널, next to Hallyeosudo cable car / luge)
gaps.why: Korea's largest tour-boat cluster: 12 vessels incl. 500-pax cruise, Hallyeosudo + Jangsado circuits (Jangsado drew 410k visitors in 2012); adjacent cable car drew 1.32M/yr. Not in payload.

gaps.name: Samcheonpo Newport Ferry Terminal (삼천포신항, Sacheon)
gaps.why: Payload's 'Samcheonpo Ferry Terminal' is paired with Yeosu (no service). Real traffic: Samcheonpo<->Jeju overnight ROPAX (Ocean Vista Jeju, 860 pax, reopened 2024) + local Sinsudo car ferry; also Sacheon ocean cable car tourist base.
